claims.text: Ferromagnetic ground states can be detected using spin-polarized scanning tunneling microscopy (SP-STM).
SP-STM is a surface-sensitive magnetic imaging method.
SP-STM can directly image local spin orientations at a material surface.
Low temperature minimizes thermal disturbances during SP-STM measurements.
Ultra-high vacuum helps maintain the surface cleanliness required for SP-STM.
A calibrated spin-polarized tip is required for the proposed measurement.
A ferromagnetic ground state is associated with aligned atomic magnetic moments and magnetic domains at the surface.
The SP-STM tunneling current is sensitive to the electron spin state and can therefore differentiate spin orientations.
Spin-dependent tunneling contrast reveals uniform spin alignment when a ferromagnetic ground state is present.
Ferromagnetic samples will exhibit uniform spin alignment and a net magnetic moment across domains in SP-STM images.
Non-ferromagnetic or paramagnetic materials will exhibit random spin contrast or no spin contrast.
SP-STM primarily probes surface magnetism rather than bulk magnetism.
Surface magnetic properties can differ from bulk magnetic properties.
Limited SP-STM sensitivity or resolution may prevent detection of subtle spin contrast.
Comparison with confirmed ferromagnetic, paramagnetic, and non-magnetic controls can test whether SP-STM reliably identifies ferromagnetic ground states.
Failure of SP-STM contrast to distinguish known ferromagnetic samples from non-ferromagnetic samples would falsify the proposed detection hypothesis.
Failure of spatially mapped spin orientation to correlate with established bulk magnetic properties would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis predicts uniform spin alignment and a net moment across domains, while also invoking magnetic domains and acknowledging that only the surface is measured. Distinct ferromagnetic domains can have different orientations, so surface domain contrast does not by itself establish uniform alignment or a net bulk moment.
